_meta.purpose: Crisis-resource corpus for locale 'en'. Loaded by ciris_engine.schemas.resources.crisis.load_crisis_registry and injected into DSDMA prompts via format_crisis_resources_block (CIRISAgent#971).
_meta.rule: HOTLINES: NEVER add or edit a hotline/text-line number without a human verifying it against an authoritative source (source=national_verified, verified=true). EMERGENCY numbers (police/ambulance/fire): emitted only under the owner's cited-sources standard of 2026-10-29 — >=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official, source=multi_source_cited (CIRISAgent#1248). A wrong crisis number is catastrophically worse than the directory fallback.

verification_notes: Base corpus. US/UK/global entries carried from the builtin registry; Ethiopia emergency entries verified May 2026 (see per-entry notes). Emergency (police/ambulance/fire) numbers for GB, IE, AU, NZ, ZA, PH added 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248): 6 of 10 meet the owner's cited-sources standard (source=multi_source_cited, emitted); the rest are staged verified=false and NOT emitted — see CRISIS_RESOURCES_VERIFICATION_NEEDED.md.

emergency_united_kingdom_999.name: Emergency services
emergency_united_kingdom_999.description: National emergency number (police, ambulance, fire, coastguard)
emergency_united_kingdom_999.validation_notes: CITED 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248) under the owner's cited-sources standard (>=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official; no human check). Sources: UK FCDO travel advice: gov.uk: "999 and 112 is the national emergency response service in the UK"; "112 is the pan-European equivalent to 999 and can be used in the UK" | AOSP eccdata (Android's emergency-number database): GB 999 types ['AMBULANCE', 'FIRE', 'POLICE']. Sources agree it reaches: ambulance, fire, police. UK FCDO page checked: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/999-and-112-the-uks-national-emergency-numbers (fetched 2026-10-29); page text: gov.uk: "999 and 112 is the national emergency response service in the UK"; "112 is the pan-European equivalent to 999 and can be used in the UK". Cross-check (not a source): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_emergency_telephone_numbers — wikipedia agrees. 'languages' = the locale this entry is staged for (en), not a verified statement of operator languages.
